card vi-flow  [decided]
werk is the one project where the product's data flow and the card status loop coincide. Do not generalize from it
why: werk's product is the planning loop. So its data flow — ideate, prototype, decide — is the same loop as open, proto, decided in log.jsonl. For any other project the two are unrelated: a payments system's data flow is not its planning statuses. This coincidence is what made the first version of #vi-sysdiag wrong.

The trap: testing the product-diagram prototype on werk itself will make a derived diagram look correct for the wrong reason. The card statuses will supply the data flow, and it will read as if the fold worked.

Test it on a second project before believing it.

The coincidence also makes the status loop itself measurable. That is a separate idea: #vi-flow-telemetry.

card kill-render  [decided]
Kill criteria render as a section right below the card, one row per criterion
why: The criteria say how this decision ends. They belong beside Options and Depends on, as a section of the card details page. They come first, so a reader sees them before the lists. A criterion has several fields, so it needs a row, and each criterion fires on its own.

Position: a section in the card details page, the first one after the hero. It sits above the "below" grid, Options, and Depends on. It has an h2 heading "Kill criteria" and a list of `.depwhy` rows, like the other sections. The hero has no badge and no kill content.

One row per criterion, two lines:
- Line 1: the ring, the state chip, the trigger chip, and on the right the fallback link to the rejected :optN node. The state sits at the left edge of every row, so a reader scans the states down one column.
- Line 2: the criterion in plain words. For a metric: source, metric, threshold, window, minimum sample. For the other forms: the reason type, or "revisit at any time". A review date shows the date.
- A fired or unmonitored row has a detail line below. Fired: when, the value, the sample size. Unmonitored: why the check failed.

Color follows the colors the map already has:
- fired uses the stale red (.depwhy.stale).
- unmonitored uses the paused grey (.depwhy.paused).
- monitored uses the neutral border.
- a decided card with no criterion uses the unchallenged ring. #kill-ask makes this state rare.

An open card with no criterion shows dashed rows with a "suggested" chip: the drafted suggestions from #kill-ask.

  -> depends_on      kill  Every decision carries kill criteria: what must become true to revisit it

  -> depends_on      werk-depwhy  Why a dependency is flagged: a section between the hero and Depends on

card vi-flow-telemetry  [decided]
The card status loop is measured from the log
why: Every status change is one timestamped event in the log, so the loop open → proto → decided can be counted, not drawn. A drawn loop goes stale; a fold over the log cannot.
subtree: 5 cards, 5 decided, 2 unchallenged

Fill the loop from the log:

- the count of cards at each status
- the median time a card holds a status before it moves
- the traffic on each arrow, including reopen, which runs backward from decided to open and is the arrow that says the plan was wrong

This is telemetry on the map, not a diagram of the product (#vi-flow).

Open: what view shows it, and which of the three numbers a person acts on.

card vi-prop  [decided]
Propagation cannot be done by asking a model
why: Single-hop validity checks recover only 6% to 11% of the invalidation chain.
subtree: 3 cards, 1 proto, 2 decided

So every card records depends_on at the moment it is created. There is no recovering the edges later.

Formally: reverse dependency closure, mark stale, re-derive in topological order, cost O(|S(v)|). This is the build-system model applied to meaning. Mark stale, never delete — deleting destroys the evidence chain.

This is a discipline cost on me, every turn, forever. If I skip it the map rots into a pretty outline.
